settings.title: The real effects of vaping
settings.content:
Learn what vaping really does to your body, not the myths, the facts.

We’ve broken it down so you can see what’s happening inside, and why quitting isn’t just willpower. It’s understanding the cycle and taking back control.

settings.title: 1. The Cycle
settings.content:
You vape to feel calm, nicotine quietly raises your stress. That spike makes you reach for another puff, then another. Over time:

• Your baseline anxiety climbs
• Your mood drops
• Your sleep gets lighter
• Your day revolves around the next hit.

It doesn’t feel like a trap until you realise you can’t relax without it.

Truth:
Nicotine gives the illusion of calm while making stress harder to control.

settings.title: 2. Dopamine – The Fake “Feel Good”
settings.content:
That calm or focus after a vape isn’t real relaxation. It’s your reward system firing on command.

What’s actually happening:
• Nicotine becomes the main thing your brain links to “feeling good”
• Natural dopamine falls, so you feel flat without it
• Cravings hit harder because your brain is chasing the chemical spike
• Normal things stop feeling rewarding

Truth:
Vaping rewires your reward system to respond only to nicotine.

Take the nicotine away and your confidence, focus, and mood start coming back.

settings.title: 3. Your Lungs
settings.content:
The “smooth” feeling means nothing. The damage starts early.

Inside your lungs:
• Airways swell and trap mucus • Alveoli (tiny air sacs) stiffen, reducing deep-breath capacity
• Immune defence weakens, so infections last longer

• Endurance drops from reduced oxygen

Truth:
Lungs start clearing in 72 hours when you stop.

Leave it long enough and some damage cannot be reversed.

settings.title: 4. Stress & Anxiety
settings.content:
The “calm” from vaping is a lie. Nicotine triggers stress pathways, not peace.

What it does:
• Dopamine spikes and crashes increase anxiety
• Cortisol rises and stays high
• Memory and learning pathways weaken
• Blood pressure and heart rate rise
• Sleep becomes lighter and less restorative
• Skin inflames and ages faster

Truth:
Every puff pushes your stress system harder.

Quit, and real calm comes back within weeks.

settings.title: 5. Your Heart
settings.content:
Nicotine hits your blood in seconds and forces your heart to work harder.

What happens:
• Blood vessels tighten
• Oxygen drops
• Arteries inflame and stiffen
• Heart muscle thickens over time
• Stroke risk rises with daily use

Truth:
Heart improvements start within two to six weeks after quitting.

settings.title: 6. Your Skin
settings.content:
Your skin reacts faster than people realise.

What Happens:
• Higher cortisol increases oil and inflammation
• Blood flow drops, so skin looks dull
• Collagen breaks down quicker, causing early lines
• Breakouts last longer because healing slows

Truth:
Your skin starts visibly recovering within weeks of quitting.

settings.title: 7. Hormones & Performance
settings.content:
Men – Testosterone, Drive, Strength

Nicotine disrupts hormone production at the source:
• Testosterone falls
• Stress hormones rise
• Muscle growth slows
• Libido drops
• Recovery gets worse

Truth:
Quit, and testosterone begins rising again within weeks.

settings.title: Women – Balance, Mood, Energy
settings.content:
Nicotine alters hormone regulation:
• Estrogen and progesterone rhythms shift
• AMH (egg reserve marker) can drop
• Bloating and fatigue increase
• Mood swings become sharper
• Gym progress slows

Truth:
Hormone balance starts returning once nicotine is out of your system.

settings.title: You don’t need another lecture, you just need a way out.
